children: HEG Ltd shares appeared to crash as much as 65 percent in morning trade on Monday, but the eye-popping decline was largely an optical effect following the company’s demerger rather than an actual collapse in shareholder value. The stock was trading around Rs 258 in morning deals, compared with Friday’s closing price of Rs 728.25. However, the appropriate comparison is with the demerger-adjusted price of around Rs 260, implying an actual decline of only about 0.8 percent.

HEG shares began trading ex-demerger on Monday as the company separated its graphite electrode business from its advanced materials and energy operations. Today, September 7 is the record date for determining shareholders eligible to receive shares in the demerged graphite business.

Under the restructuring, the existing listed company has been renamed HEG Advanced Materials Ltd and retains the advanced materials, battery energy solutions and green power businesses. Bhilwara Energy Ltd has also been amalgamated into the company.
Meanwhile, the graphite electrode business has been transferred to HEG Graphite Ltd, which is proposed to be renamed HEG Ltd and separately listed as a pure-play graphite electrode company.

Why does HEG stock show a 65% fall today?

The apparent plunge reflects the removal of the value of the graphite electrode business from the price of the existing listed company. Friday's Rs 728.25 closing price represented HEG before the demerger adjustment, while Monday's trading price represents HEG Advanced Materials after the graphite business was carved out.

Shareholders have not simply lost the difference. Investors holding HEG Advanced Materials shares on the September 7 record date are entitled to receive one fully paid-up share of HEG Graphite for every share they hold in HEG Advanced Materials.

The graphite company's shares are expected to list separately in the second half of October. Until then, the value attributable to those shares will not be reflected in the market price of HEG Advanced Materials, making a direct comparison between Friday's and Monday's quoted prices misleading.

Before the demerger, HEG had a market capitalisation of more than Rs 11,500 crore at Friday's close. The post-demerger listed entity was valued at more than Rs 5,000 crore in Monday morning trade. The balance will effectively be represented by the separately listed graphite business once its shares begin trading.
On a pre-demerger basis, HEG shares had gained around 17 percent in 2026 through Friday, substantially outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen around 9 percent over the same period.
What HEG shareholders get after the demerger
The demerger follows a 1:1 entitlement ratio: shareholders will receive one Rs 2 face-value share of HEG Graphite for every Rs 2 face-value share held in HEG Advanced Materials as of the record date.

As part of the broader composite scheme, Bhilwara Energy has been merged into HEG Advanced Materials. Riju Jhunjhunwala is set to lead HEG Advanced Materials as Chairman, Managing Director and CEO, while Ravi Jhunjhunwala will serve as Chairman, Managing Director and CEO of HEG Graphite.
